Slum Linear Layout

The missing patrolman, laid out from your scenario as seven streamed sections: a night street with people still out, an eskinita, the yard where the patrol car is hidden, then the compound. That's knocked-through row houses, a covered alley, a bodega, the holding house and a three-level trap house at the end. Every street and alley bends, or has something standing in it, within about 25 m, and no room or yard is deeper than 18 m. The longest sightline in any fight space is 24.8 m, and the walk-around street's is 25.8 m. Both were measured on this plan with a 1.2 m-wide line. Fights follow the room-encounter rules: 2–5 waiting, waves topping up to 4, never more than 6 in one fight. Arms are .45 pistols, revolvers and shotguns only. Story beats are inspects: the car one starts the first big fight, and the documents one ends the level. There are no drops: every section border is a swinging door (the eskinita's mouth is a bend), every way through goes both ways, and the height changes are steps.

Trap house · three levels

15 × 18 m · storeys 4 m (3.8 m clear) · the wooden storey 3.6 m clear · grey = the floor below

Built like a trap house: a hollow-block ground storey, a plastered and painted +4, and a plywood-and-tin storey on top with its own wooden stair. Doors are knocked out to 2.25 m, there's a gallery round the double-height hall, and a terrace on the +4 roof.

You see the hall twice. You fight in it from below (F9), then walk the gallery above it on the way to the bunks (F11). The kitchen's wooden stair comes up into the staging room, where F12 is the last fight. The two small rooms off it hold the photo corner and the documents.

“Kills or drives off”: F12's survivors break for the terrace and cross a plank to the neighbour's roof, then the plank falls. That's optional new tech (a scripted flee). Without it, F12 is simply a fight to the last man.

Sections + streaming

one small persistent map · each section an _Art and a _Gameplay sublevel

Loaded: the section you're in and the ones either side. Every border is a swinging door (the eskinita's mouth is a bend), and every way through goes both ways: no drops. Whichever way you walk, crossing into a section loads the next one beyond it and unloads the one furthest behind. A border door stays shut until the section behind it is loaded, and unloading waits until you're a few metres past a door, so stepping back and forth through it doesn't reload anything. A section remembers what's done (fights, pickups, inspects) when it unloads, so walking back never brings the dead back. A death reloads only the current section's _Gameplay from its last checkpoint, never the map. Every border is a door or a bend, so no two sections that aren't neighbours can see each other.

In place of the drops (2026-11-08), with no building resized: 2→3 is a door in the yard wall at the eskinita's level, then a railed landing and steps down into the yard, with the car in view from the landing (the garage roof's back edge has to clear it: about 4.2 m at the wall). In section 4, H4's floor hole is now a stair with a half landing, inside the back room. 5→6 is the bodega's back door, then steps down 1.8 m through the passage, their foot coming through a doorway into the guard room. The ground heights stay as they were: the eskinita at +1.8, the holding house at −1.8.

The generator has to learn

  1. Levels as data. The split I put off earlier: a shared building library, and level files like this JSON. The arena must still come out identical.
  2. Rooms inside houses, storey by storey: partition walls (hollow block, plywood, tarp), plastered or painted inside faces, and a paint per room.
  3. Openings: 1 m doors, 2.25 m doors, 3 m knock-throughs with broken block edges, a garage opening, open-fronted plywood rooms. The shell's windows also have to read from inside: check that the AsiaSlum wall pieces have inside faces.
  4. Floors: slabs with stairwells, a double-height hall with a railed gallery, and a wooden top storey.
  5. Stairs indoors: concrete flights at least 1.8 m wide, a stair that turns at a half landing (H4), and a steep wooden one.
  6. Ground heights: the eskinita at +1.8 and the holding house at −1.8, with steps between (a stair's foot can sit off the floor's datum: z0), railed landings, and a doorway with no door (open).
  7. 3 m eskinitas. The arena is all 4.5 m alleys, so wires, laundry, pipes and AC units need spacing rules that fit.
  8. One sublevel per section for the art, plus the gameplay actors written into each section's _Gameplay.
  9. Night: the lamps, bulbs and tubes lit (STREET_LIGHTS_ON), and bulbs and tubes in the rooms. That's the Deck cost to measure first.

New gameplay it needs

  • Inspects (yours, coming): a prompt, a look, a line or subtitle, and events. I3 saves CP2 and then starts F1; I8 ends the level through ALevelExitTrigger::Fire(), which already exists.
  • Section streaming both ways, and checkpoints: a border door that holds until the section behind it is loaded, and sections that remember what's done.
  • A fight started by an event rather than a volume (F1 on I3; F8 as you leave the cells).
  • Civilians on the street, up to 12, no fighting. What you can do with them is still undecided.
  • Optional: a scripted flee for F12's survivors.

Layout calls I made

  • The car's lane is gated at both ends. It's the car's route, never yours, and it's why you go round.
  • Section borders are swinging doors you can go back through, not drops (your call, 2026-11-08). Nothing locks behind you.
  • No fight in the cells. The reveal stays quiet, with F7 before it and F8 after.
  • Pallets inside the bodega door cut what would be a 37 m line from the alley's end.
  • CP2 saves after the car inspect, so a death in F1 doesn't replay the reveal.

Open — yours to call

  • The level's name (a story level, so no _Arena).
  • Is the patrolman's body at the car, and where?
  • How Navarro arrives, and whether he starts with a .45 or a revolver (the plan assumes a .45).
  • What the clues are at I1, I2 and I7 (my suggestions are marked).
  • Navarro's lines at each inspect: voice, subtitles, or none.
  • Who the civilians are and what you can do with them, and who the gunmen are.
  • “Drives off”: a scripted escape, or kill them all.
  • Whether any door should lock behind you for a story reason. The plan has none, so you can walk back to the street.
  • The exact child's items (your examples are used as given).
